clue.text: Got held…

definitions.meaning: to have got something is to have obtained it safely
held fast, fixed firmly in place

explanation.surface: A terse report that someone has been caught and detained.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: obtaining something and fastening it firmly are each meanings of the past tense of the verb.

clue.text: Lashes sergeants with them

definitions.meaning: strokes from a whip, which leave welts
a sergeant wears three chevrons on the sleeve as badges of rank

explanation.surface: A grim picture of NCOs flogging soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both welts from whipping and the bands of cloth that mark military rank.

clue.text: A number in the M East find Zeno & Aristotle's first piece of music

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
Aden is a port city in the Middle East, in Yemen

indicators.note: first takes the opening letters of the two philosophers' names

explanation.surface: Somebody in the Middle East finds a tune linked to two Greek thinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: An elaborate solo passage in a concerto, usually near the end of a movement, is this kind of musical piece.

clue.text: We want him to be first home and back

definitions.text: We want him to be first home and back

parts.words: We want him to be first home and back
parts.note: punters backing a runner want it to finish first, and backing means betting on

explanation.surface: Someone hoping a man wins the race home and returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' seems to mean return, but it means bet on: punters back the horse they want to win.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse bred and trained for racing, which bettors back to win.

clue.text: Very much wanted to be a knight. Indeed!

annotationWithheld.why: Very much wanted to be a knight. Indeed! (7): SIR goes inside DEED, but the single printed word 'Indeed' would have to be both the container DEED and its insertion indicator 'In'.
annotationWithheld.clue: Very much wanted to be a knight. Indeed!

clue.text: And fastened, being in warped state

definitions.meaning: done up with a clasp, as a belt or shoe is
bent out of shape, crumpled under pressure

explanation.surface: Something tied down that has also been bent out of true.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb to buckle covers both clasping a strap shut and bending or collapsing under strain.

clue.text: If so, well and good!

parts.note: a child who has done this has been good, and the phrase well and good puns on behaving well

explanation.surface: A shrug of acceptance: if that happens, fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well and good' is an idiom of acceptance; read literally it describes conducting oneself well.
explanation.definitionFit: To have behaved is to have acted properly and well, as a good child does.

clue.text: Complaint that it's cold?

parts.note: a complaint is an ailment, and a minor feverish cold is caught this way

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about the low temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grumble, but it means a minor illness.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a coldness in the air and a mild illness with shivering.

clue.text: Hard hearts open and reveal lovers inside

definitions.text: Hard hearts open and reveal lovers inside

parts.words: Hard hearts open and reveal lovers inside
parts.note: heart-shaped metal pendants hinge open to show portraits of sweethearts

explanation.surface: Cold-hearted people softening and showing their romantic side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard hearts' suggests callous people; here they are literal metal hearts worn on a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Small hinged pendants worn on a necklace, often heart-shaped, holding a picture or lock of hair.

clue.text: Hates Davis-cup leader getting set, set and set!

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
the last set means arranged, so the two earlier copies of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tennis player loathes the endless sets of a Davis Cup match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link. The final 'set' is not more fodder: it means arranged, so the two earlier copies are shuffled behind the Davis Cup initial.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe intensely, a strong synonym for hating.

clue.text: Gets down snooker ball, then miscues

parts.note: the red is the commonest ball on a snooker table
read as mis-cues: the letters of cues set amiss, giving this rearrangement

explanation.surface: A snooker player pots a red and then fluffs the next shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets down' looks like crouching at the table; it means lowers. The prefix mis- in 'miscues' signals the jumbling of the word it is attached to.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce something is to bring it down or lower it, as one gets down a figure.

clue.text: Locks away instruction to hippie recruit!

definitions.text: Locks away instruction to hippie recruit!

parts.words: Locks away instruction to hippie recruit
parts.note: a long-haired recruit is ordered to lose his locks, as army recruits are shorn

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant tells a long-haired newcomer to get rid of his flowing hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks away' looks like imprisoning something; here locks are hair and away means off.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting hair short is exactly what a newly enlisted soldier is ordered to have.

clue.text: Mix your drinks to get so drunk?

definitions.text: Mix your drinks to get so drunk?

parts.words: Mix your drinks to get so drunk
parts.note: a bowl of mixed drinks gives the first half of the phrase meaning dazed, as a boxer is after too many blows

explanation.surface: A warning that mixing drinks leaves you very intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch-drunk describes a boxer dazed from blows, not a drinker; the bowl of mixed drinks supplies the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A party drink made by mixing spirits, fruit juice and spices in a bowl.

clue.text: They, go round killing people

definitions.meaning: things that rotate or turn about an axis
pistols with revolving chambers, weapons that kill

explanation.surface: A grim statement about people who wander around committing murder.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both things that rotate and the classic cylinder handguns of Westerns.

clue.text: Took lead in film "The Badge of Sheriff Scarlet"

parts.note: a Western sheriff wears a star-shaped badge
scarlet is a shade of red

explanation.surface: An actor headlined a Western with a title about a sheriff's badge.
explanation.definitionFit: To have starred in a film is to have played its leading role.

clue.text: Swears he throws people out of offices!

definitions.meaning: testifies under oath, as a witness making a statement
removes rulers or officials from power

explanation.surface: Someone cursing while ejecting staff from their rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both giving sworn testimony and ousting someone from a position of power.

clue.text: Washington State created in 1789, as it were

definitions.text: Washington State created in 1789, as it were

parts.words: Washington State created in 1789, as it were
parts.note: Washington was made head of the new United States in 1789, not a state of the union

explanation.surface: A history fact about when Washington State was founded.
explanation.walkthrough: Washington State joined the union in 1889; in 1789 George Washington became the first head of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The elected head of state of a republic such as the United States.

clue.text: Had enough of Peter, the French lunatic

indicators.note: a lunatic is crazy, so these letters go wild and rearrange

parts.note: le is the French masculine form of the

explanation.surface: A complaint about being fed up with a mad Frenchman called Peter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being replete means being full, having eaten or had as much as one needs.

clue.text: Said no, but joined up again

explanation.surface: Someone declined, yet signed up a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means declined, and split as re-fused it also means fused together anew.

clue.text: Harbour charged little bit

parts.note: a port is a harbour
an ion is a small electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: A harbour that charged a small fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion is a part or share of something, a piece or bit.

clue.text: Quite another word meaning the same in common parlance

definitions.text: Quite another word meaning the same in common parlance

parts.words: Quite another word meaning the same in common parlance
parts.note: people say Quite! to agree, and the answer is the everyday word used the same way

explanation.surface: A note on a word with a synonym in everyday speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite' looks like an adverb on 'another'; it is the agreeing exclamation 'Quite!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are spoken in agreement, meaning precisely so, just as you say.

clue.text: Each has the odd cat

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters are put in a strange new order

explanation.surface: A claim that every person keeps a peculiar pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is just a link; 'odd' rearranges EACH plus THE.
explanation.definitionFit: This spotted African big cat is famous as the fastest animal on land.

parts.note: split as 100, 0, 1000, 1, 100, the Roman numerals C, M, I, C with a round 0 standing for the letter O
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A string of digits presented as a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comical is amusing and makes people laugh.

clue.text: It took ages to decide the winner of this 28 across

definitions.text: It took ages to decide the winner of this 28 across

parts.words: It took ages to decide the winner of this 28 across
parts.note: in this scheme of chance the last surviving subscriber collects the whole fund, which may take decades

explanation.surface: A complaint about a slow prize draw.
explanation.walkthrough: A tontine is an annuity scheme where shares pass to survivors until the last one alive takes all, so 'ages' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: An investment scheme in which the last surviving member takes the pot, a kind of gamble on longevity.

clue.text: Physician, heal thyself; result, in part!

definitions.text: Physician, heal thyself; result, in part!

indicators.note: in part says only a portion of the quoted words is taken, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: The proverb about doctors curing themselves, and its outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a physician who heals himself becomes well.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well and free of illness is the result of successful healing.

clue.text: If backing genuine member, it's a danger-signal

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word if is read the other way round

parts.note: genuine means real
an arm is a limb, one of the body's members

explanation.surface: A conditional remark about a true member of a club raising a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell or siren warning people of a blaze is a signal of danger.

clue.text: Bars undercarriages having wheels

definitions.meaning: the parts of a vehicle's underside on which wheels turn

explanation.surface: Prohibitions on landing gear fitted with wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: These rods on which wheels spin are bars, and part of every wheeled undercarriage.

clue.text: St Columba founded monastery here in 1 BC. Greeks inhabited it

indicators.note: the numeral is placed inside the island's name

parts.note: Saint Columba founded his monastery on the Scottish island of Iona in 563
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A history note about a saint's monastery and ancient Greek settlers.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is a small island in the Hebrides, off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient coastal region of Asia Minor was settled by Greek colonists before Christ.

clue.text: In which to cook up murder within the group

indicators.note: within says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a set is a group of things
to murder is to kill

explanation.surface: A plot about a killing carried out by a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A frying pan, a utensil for cooking food on a stove.

clue.text: He can dispense with his qualifications

definitions.text: He can dispense with his qualifications

parts.words: He can dispense with his qualifications
parts.note: dispense with seems to mean do without, but here it means hand out medicines, which this professional is qualified to do

explanation.surface: A man so able he no longer needs his certificates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispense with' usually means do without; here it means make up prescriptions, using his qualifications.
explanation.definitionFit: A British pharmacist, who is licensed to make up and sell prescribed drugs.

clue.text: Running the country business for such a family

definitions.text: Running the country business for such a family

parts.words: Running the country business for such a family
parts.note: a ruling house passes the governing of the nation down its line, like a family firm

explanation.surface: A family that runs a rural firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country business' suggests a farm or village shop; it means governing the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A succession of rulers from one family line, such as the Tudors or the Ming.

clue.text: Something for nothing? Just the ticket!

definitions.text: Something for nothing? Just the ticket!

parts.words: Something for nothing? Just the ticket
parts.note: a prize draw promises a reward for next to nothing, and all you need to buy is a ticket

explanation.surface: Delight at a free gift that is exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the ticket' is an idiom for exactly right, but taken literally a ticket is all you hold in a draw.
explanation.definitionFit: A game of chance in which numbered tickets are drawn to win prizes.
